source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. First, make sure you have an HTTPS server available and that you already know the URL of the image file.
2. Connect to the target server's BMC using SSH or otherwise.
3. After logging in to BMC, enter the OpenBMC console.
4. Image mount using OpenBMC's Web GUI. From the remote console interface, select Media -> Activate, then select Media -> Mount virtual media.
5. In the ""Mount Media File from Network"" option, enter the URL of your HTTP image file, for example: https://myserver.mycompany.com/media/myCD.ISO.
HTTPs — https://<URL>/<file path>/<image name>
6. From the ""Local Media Mounted"" section, select your software format (probably CD/DVD), then click ""Browse"" to find the software file, click ""Open"", then click ""Mount"".
7. Once it's done, you can go into the mounted ISO and do things like install an operating system.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: HTTP share/URL with a reachable HTTP image + BMC web + OS block tools
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Mount image via HTTPS: mount the install image via HTTP from the BMC web -> Media -> Mount Virtual Media (HTTP share/URL: ${VM_SHARE:?operator must set the virtual media share or server url}/${VM_PATH:?operator must set the path on the share}/${VM_IMAGE:?operator must set the image file name}), then confirm the image appears as a boot/block device sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "lsblk 2>&1; dmesg | tail -n 15 2>&1"; state-changing mount.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the OS block-device list + BMC web mount status so the user confirms the HTTP image mounted cleanly and is accessible.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: mounting an image shares it to the host and can autostart the OS; use a user-designated image URL and unmount after.

original_test_intent: Validate HTTPS-hosted BMC virtual-media mounting, remote-console connectivity and host CD-ROM exposure, with an unclear reference to OS auto-install.
original_method: Engineer uses OpenBMC WebUI to mount a network image and may enter its installer; OS tools inspect the exposed device.
manual_activity: After scope correction, an engineer must operate/observe WebUI and remote console; any installation requires separate destructive authorization.
required_inputs: HTTPS URL, CA/auth and immutable image hash
Expected virtual device and console state
safety_requirements: Do not disable certificate verification or use mutable/untrusted media.
Do not boot/install/write disks without explicit scope and target.
Use trusted access; deactivate media and verify removal.
No automatic retry; preserve unexpected installer/device evidence.
agent_execution_scope: After correction, validate HTTPS/image metadata, collect read-only device/log evidence and analyze manual WebUI artifacts.
Do not operate WebUI, install an OS or issue the verdict.
engineer_actions: Resolve scope/security and operate the approved WebUI flow.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Generic HTTP variables, sshpass and lsblk cannot prove HTTPS trust, remote-console success or safe installer scope.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Split a trusted HTTPS mount-only flow from any boot/install plan; preserve vendor WebUI operation and explicit deactivation.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: HTTPS/HTTP wording, WebUI steps, auto-install criterion and 15/5-minute values remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Define a certificate-validated, immutable mount-only test; put boot/install in a separate disk-targeted plan.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: BMC with documented HTTPS virtual media.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds trust, image identity and scope separation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Retains mount coverage without falsely claiming install coverage.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Bootable media can overwrite host storage.

project_override_considerations: A narrower approved mount-only result is project-plan completion, not completion of an undefined auto-install claim.
expected_evidence: Approved scope and HTTPS trust chain

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Source says HTTPS but calls it HTTP, omits numbered criteria, and conflates reversible mount/device visibility with auto-install.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Mount and install have incompatible safety contracts; TLS/image trust and disk target are also undefined, so execution would guess a destructive end state.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on BLOCKED for semantic/safety reasons.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Does not block merely for missing URL or WebUI attendance.

review_improvement: Separates TLS trust, media exposure and installation.
independent_technical_reasoning: A mounted CD-ROM can be verified safely, but the same source also expects an installer without target protection. Until the owner selects the end state, neither manual nor automated execution is safe.
